title: Tight Quantum Collision Bound for Single-Round Sponges
summary: For single-round sponges, a tight quantum collision bound is known when rate is at most capacity, but the optimal bound above capacity remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine the tight quantum collision-resistance bound for a single-round sponge with $n$-bit outputs, rate $r$, and capacity $c$, especially in the regime $r>c$. The available bound has fourth-power dependence on the number $q$ of quantum queries and is unlikely to be tight because the BHT algorithm finds a collision using $O(2^{n/3})$ queries. Quantum indifferentiability yields a tight collision-resistance bound when $r\le c$, whereas only a first nontrivial bound is known when $r>c$; the unresolved task is to characterize the optimal collision success bound or query complexity in that regime.

scope.domain: Quantum collision resistance and attack complexity for single-round sponge hash constructions.
parameters: r: sponge rate, with the unresolved regime defined by r exceeding c
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the optimal collision-success bound or quantum query complexity when the sponge rate exceeds its capacity.

citations.label: Quantum Lifting for Invertible Permutations and Ideal Ciphers

progress.summary: The source presents a bound with fourth-power query dependence as the first nontrivial result when rate exceeds capacity, while the BHT attack indicates that it is unlikely to be tight. It contrasts this with a tight bound when rate is at most capacity.
citation_labels: Alexandru Cojocaru et al., Quantum Lifting for Invertible Permutations and Ideal Ciphers
